changelog.name: v2.3.6
changelog.body:
**TL;DR**
Improved UI/UX design in both create and history page, and improved tap-to-focus.
- History rows swipe like Android 16+ notifications: neighbours cling to the row being pulled, it comes loose with a click, and the vibration grows as it is pulled
- While reordering favorites, dragging one near the top or bottom scrolls the list toward the favorites out of view
- Turned sideways, the create page shows the code beside the controls, and it offers the same apps as result cards
- A tapped focus lets go as soon as the view changes, even before the camera has finished focusing
- Fixed some issues

<details>
<summary>Full changelog</summary>

feat: a history row follows the finger at half its pace while the rows up to two away lean with it and the rows around it round toward it, with ticks that grow stronger as it is pulled; at 80dp it comes loose with a click and follows the finger, rejoining with another click below 64dp. A row let go once loose deletes or favorites unless flung back, a row still attached acts when flung away at 500dp/s or faster, and the background a swipe reveals takes the row's shape
feat: while reordering favorites, holding one within 48dp of the top bar or the navigation bar scrolls the list toward the favorites reaching past that edge, faster the closer it is held, until the first or last favorite is 48dp inside; the held row stays under the finger and the top bar keeps its size
feat: turned sideways, the create page puts the code in one half and the controls in the other, and a tap on the code shows it over the whole window
changed: a swipe on a history row acts from 80dp of travel or a quick flick, in place of half the row's width
changed: the create page offers apps ranked as result cards rank them, including the app the system opens a link in directly
changed: a tapped focus lets go at once when the view changes in a way focusing and metering do not change it, even before focusing finishes, and the camera returns to focusing by itself; the camera's own scene change report counts only once the exposure has settled
changed: every message replaces the one on screen instead of waiting for it to time out
changed: the reset button on the scanner vibrates as it is pressed, like the other buttons
changed: the ferry page is titled "Opening codes"
changed: the settings page's ferry entry and the history entries centre their icons and trailing content
fixed: a delete or favorite decided by a swipe is carried out even when the row is scrolled out of view before it finishes
fixed: the apps on the create page keep their places while their group fades out, instead of jumping when it comes back
fixed: the more formats chip on the create page takes the colours of the other unselected formats
chore: FerryQR declares VIBRATE for vibrations of a chosen strength; devices without vibration primitives tick more often instead of more strongly
chore: capture results reach tap to focus through the session config's Camera2 interop, replacing the deprecated preview extender

</details>

changelog.name: v2.3.5
changelog.body:
**TL;DR (changes since v2.3.3)**
Tap to focus, smarter handoff to other apps, and a reorganised ferry page.
- Tap the viewfinder to focus, with a focus box that stays until the camera lets go of that focus
- Cards lead with "Open in" the app that opens a link, an app link or a two-factor key directly
- Xiaomi Account sign-in and Mi Home device codes open in their apps from history and the create page too
- The ferry page splits into apps that need the module and everything that works without it, including system features and default apps
- Fixed a crash when scanning Wi-Fi Easy Connect codes, and fixed some issues

<details>
<summary>Full changelog</summary>

feat: a tap on the viewfinder while scanning focuses and meters there; a focus box with a tick in the middle of each side closes in on the point, and fades out once the camera lets go of that focus: after five seconds, when the camera sees a new scene, when a code waiting to be read takes over after three seconds, or when the scan ends
fixed: pressing reset again plays its haptic at once, since each scan message now replaces the snackbar on screen instead of waiting for the one before to time out

</details>

changelog.name: v2.3.4
changelog.body:
**TL;DR**
Smarter handoff to other apps and a reorganised ferry page.
- Cards lead with "Open in" the app that opens a link, an app link or a two-factor key directly
- Xiaomi Account sign-in and Mi Home device codes open in their apps from history and the create page too
- The ferry page splits into apps that need the module and everything that works without it, including system features and default apps
- Fixed a crash when scanning Wi-Fi Easy Connect codes, and fixed some issues

<details>
<summary>Full changelog</summary>

feat: result cards for links, app links and two-factor keys lead with "Open in" the app the system opens them in without asking, such as one with a verified App Link
feat: Xiaomi Account sign-in and Mi Home device codes get "Open in Xiaomi Account" and "Open in Mi Home" on their cards, in history and on the create page, not only when scanned
feat: a card for a code that only its own app opens, such as a Xiaomi sign-in, says when that app is not installed, while still offering the browser and the general apps
feat: the ferry page has two tabs, With module and Without module; the latter lists the apps FerryQR reaches through their own entries, the system features for eSIM, passkeys and digital credentials, Wi-Fi networks and Wi-Fi Easy Connect with whether the device supports each, and the app the system opens contacts, events, email, SMS, phone numbers and map locations in
changed: with the module working in WeChat, Meituan or DiDi, their links and app links go through the module first, ahead of the app's own App Links and schemes
changed: "Open in browser" opens the default browser even for a link with a verified App Link, instead of the app that holds it
changed: app link cards say that no app can open the link only when none can, and offer the app that registers the link
changed: apps on the ferry page are sorted by name in the display language
changed: the settings page lists the ferry page under a Ferrying header, with the summary "Supported apps, module status and ferry methods"
changed: the module tab's intro no longer mentions Alipay, which is listed in the Without module tab instead
fixed: scanning a Wi-Fi Easy Connect code no longer crashes, including on systems where the Wi-Fi state permission is turned off
chore: FerryQR queries for apps with links of any scheme, passkey handlers and the contacts and calendar apps, to name the app each code goes to, and declares ACCESS_WIFI_STATE to ask whether the device supports Wi-Fi Easy Connect
chore: every way a code reaches another app is either an active ferry, adapted by hand, or a passive ferry the system resolves, ranked in one place for automatic opening, cards and the create page

</details>

changelog.name: v2.3.3
changelog.body:
**TL;DR**
Several UI/UX improvements.
- Favorites are picked up with a long press anywhere while reordering, with refined animation.
- The settings pages are laid out as Material 3 Expressive lists with even spacing
- On the create page, the keyboard closes together with the format picker opening
- Updated dependencies and fixed some issues

<details>
<summary>Full changelog</summary>

changed: while reordering favorites, a long press anywhere on one picks it up and its handle picks it up at once; the lifted row takes the expressive dragged look and glides into its place when let go short of it
changed: the favorite menu keeps only moving to the top, while screen readers keep moving up and down during reordering
changed: settings rows are expressive segmented list items whose corners morph when pressed, and the settings, open-in and history pages share one set of margins and gaps
changed: on the open-in page, each app's buttons run across the whole row under its name and status
changed: switch rows in the settings are centred vertically
changed: the more formats chip on the create page is an assist chip, announced as a button by screen readers
changed: the Chinese tag for a code's own format reads 原始
fixed: unchecked toggle buttons in setting rows stand out from the row instead of blending into it
fixed: opening the format picker while typing on the create page closes the keyboard in the same motion, so the code no longer jumps to its new size
chore: AGP 9.6.0-alpha05, Compose BOM alpha 2026.11.01 (material3 1.6.0-alpha01), lifecycle 2.12.0-alpha06, CameraX 1.7.0, core-ktx 1.20.0-alpha01 and Gradle 9.9.2
chore: the text fields on the create page and in the rename dialog use TextFieldState in place of deprecated overloads

</details>

changelog.name: v2.3.2
changelog.body:
**TL;DR**
- Two-factor authentication codes open in an authenticator app, or show a card to copy the key
- Each kind of sensitive content can be kept out of history
- Passkey requests are named for what they ask

<details>
<summary>Full changelog</summary>

feat: two-factor authentication codes go straight to an authenticator app; their card shows the service, account and type, keeps the key out of sight, and offers to add, copy the key or account, and copy or share the link, with a note on what the key gives away
feat: without an authenticator app that adds keys from links, the two-factor card says so and leads with copying the key
feat: the settings choose for each kind of sensitive content whether a scan is kept in history: Wi-Fi passwords, boarding passes, eSIM activation codes, passkey requests and two-factor keys
feat: passkey requests are named for what they ask, such as signing in or creating a passkey, in history, favorites and their card
changed: eSIM activation codes, passkey requests and two-factor keys are no longer kept in history unless switched on in the settings; favoriting one still keeps it
changed: the settings for opening codes in other apps have a page of their own, and the settings follow the order of use
fixed: history titles without spaces, such as links and keys, fill their first line instead of leaving a short piece like "FIDO:/" alone on it

</details>

changelog.name: v2.3.1
changelog.body:
**TL;DR (changes since v2.2.1)**
- Create codes in any of 13 formats, with the right one suggested
- Boarding passes open as a readable card
- Barcodes enlarge by tilting, growing taller or going full screen sideways

<details>
<summary>Full changelog</summary>

fixed: switching the format of an enlarged code in history shows the new format at once instead of the old one

</details>

changelog.body:
**TL;DR**
- Create codes in any of 13 formats, with the right one suggested
- Boarding passes open as a readable card
- Barcodes enlarge by tilting, growing taller or going full screen sideways

<details>
<summary>Full changelog</summary>

feat: the create page draws every format ZXing writes, 13 in all, and starts from a suggested one: PDF417 for boarding passes, EAN-13 or UPC-A for numbers with a valid check digit, QR otherwise
feat: a format picker previews the text in every format and explains why a format cannot hold it, such as a wrong digit count or check digit
feat: an optional setting makes the create page start from the format chosen last time
feat: a long press on a code in history draws it in another format for the reader at hand, while the entry keeps its own
feat: history draws barcodes such as EAN-13 and Code 128 again in their own format instead of as a QR code
feat: boarding pass codes get a card with each flight's route, date, seat, class and sequence number, the booking reference, the passenger, frequent flyer and bag tag numbers, the raw content and a privacy note
feat: barcodes and PDF417 enlarge by tilting along the diagonal, by growing taller with their bars drawn again rather than stretched, or over the whole screen turned sideways, as a setting chooses
feat: an optional setting turns the screen to full brightness while a code is enlarged
feat: favorites can be reordered in history by dragging, from the menu or with accessibility actions, and the app shortcuts follow the order
feat: passkey requests older than five minutes are marked as likely expired, and passkey, eSIM and Wi-Fi Easy Connect cards offer to try again
fixed: an enlarged code fits the screen when the phone is turned or the window is resized
fixed: result cards about as tall as the screen follow a swipe down from anywhere on them instead of shaking under the finger
fixed: passkey, eSIM and Wi-Fi Easy Connect cards say the system did not take a code only after a camera scan was offered to it
fixed: sharing from a history card leaves the card open, as sharing the code image already did
fixed: turning the screen in history no longer closes an open card

</details>

changelog.name: v2.2.1
changelog.body:
fixed: swiping a history entry acts only once the row has moved halfway across, so a short quick flick no longer deletes or stars it by accident
changed: the tick and the colored background during a swipe mark the point past which letting go deletes the entry or changes its favorite; flinging the row back from there cancels the swipe

changelog.body:
feat: the LSPosed module opens codes in DiDi and Meituan as well as WeChat, such as bike codes and Meituan, Dianping and Maoyan links
feat: mini program codes reach WeChat in the form its own scanner reads them, so the mini program opens at once
feat: a settings page shows whether the module works in each app, and sets how each app takes codes: directly, or shown to its camera
feat: the module's state comes from LSPosed itself, and an updated FerryQR takes effect in running apps without restarting them
feat: a toast confirms each code ferried to another app
feat: without the module, a code still in front of the camera opens its app's scanner for a second scan, and other codes show a card with the actions available
feat: DiDi and Meituan links that the apps register as App Links open in them directly
feat: WeChat red packet codes and more WeChat Pay links open in WeChat
feat: cards, history, favorites and shortcuts name what a code is, such as "Meituan bike [no.]", "WeChat Pay code", a Wi-Fi network or a contact
feat: mini program codes in history are named by their content as WeChat reads it
feat: result cards show save, copy and share under the code instead of in a long press menu, and put all actions on one line when they fit
feat: history, the create page and settings open as pages of their own, with the system's predictive back animation
feat: the create page keeps its actions under the code, offers the same apps as result cards, and settles in one motion as the keyboard opens or closes
fixed: the create page toolbar no longer jumps sideways when the offered apps change
fixed: the share button no longer flashes as it becomes available
fixed: the favorite star on the create page matches the buttons beside it
fixed: a card opened from a favorite shortcut right after start offers the apps the module works in
fixed: the save and copy icons look as large and as bold as the star beside them
changed: DiDi and Meituan need to be ticked in FerryQR's scope in LSPosed, and restarted once, to take codes through the module
changed: the create page offers apps only for links, the same as result cards, and no longer for plain text
changed: the scanner no longer shows a notice when the module is active in WeChat; the settings page and the toast after each handoff show it instead

changelog.name: v2.1.0
changelog.body:
feat: codes can be kept as favorites with the star on result cards and the create page, or by swiping a history entry right
feat: favorites stay at the top of history, can be renamed, fold away when there are more than four, and are kept when history is cleared
feat: opening a favorite draws its code again, and tapping the code enlarges it for another phone to scan, with PDF417 turning as it grows
feat: up to four favorites can be added to the app shortcuts from the long press menu in history
feat: history entries can be deleted by swiping left, with undo, and a long press opens a menu of actions
feat: the create page keeps its actions in a floating toolbar and shares the code as an image to any app
feat: history and favorites are included in Android backup
fixed: messages on the create page appear above the keyboard instead of behind it
fixed: scan controls, hints, the camera permission panel and image results fit narrow screens and large fonts
fixed: a back gesture cancelled from history or the create page no longer leaves part of the camera visible and stops later back gestures from working

changelog.name: v2.0.2
changelog.body:
feat: QR codes that the quick read misses, such as small, tilted or blurred ones, get a deeper read at full resolution and a second decoder, wherever they are in view
feat: codes in view are reported together, so a QR code and a mini program code side by side both appear in the picker
feat: mini program codes that cannot be read join the picker beside the other codes, from the camera and from images
feat: the camera focuses and meters on a code that is not read yet, and zooms toward small codes of any kind
feat: small codes farther from the camera are found sooner
feat: images and screenshots are searched more thoroughly, finding mini program codes next to QR codes and small codes on full pages

changelog.name: v2.0.0
changelog.body:
breaking: the package name is now io.github.lcebot.ferryqr, as LSPosed modules expect, so 2.0.0 installs as a separate app

feat: read WeChat mini program codes, show their content and open them in WeChat
feat: optional LSPosed helper that hands scanned WeChat codes to WeChat's scanner directly, without aiming again or choosing between several codes; it only hooks Android camera APIs inside WeChat
feat: with the helper, result cards and history open WeChat codes in WeChat instead of asking for another scan
feat: mini program codes that are located but cannot be read are offered to WeChat, from the camera and from images
feat: open generated text in Alipay, and in WeChat with the helper
feat: WeChat and Alipay actions show the apps' own icons
feat: revised wording in English and Chinese

readme:
# FerryQR

A privacy-first QR scanner for Android that ferries each code to the right app. Where most scanners stop at the text of a code, FerryQR hands the code to the app or system feature that can act on it.

[中文说明](https://github.com/lcebot/ferryqr/blob/main/README_zh.md)

## Features

- **Opens codes in their own apps:** Links go to the app that handles them; Wi-Fi, contacts, events, passkeys, eSIMs, phone numbers, messages, email and map locations go to the matching part of the phone. FerryQR also reads some specific codes and shows their content, so far the information in boarding pass codes.
- **Strong scanning:** The advanced scanning found in Alipay and WeChat, such as automatic zoom and picking one of several codes, is here too. Images on the phone can be scanned by sharing them to FerryQR or opening them with it, and a screenshot shared to FerryQR quickly reads a code on the screen.
- **One scanner in place of many:** Codes meant for a particular app, WeChat mini program codes included, open straight in that app after a scan in FerryQR, so its own scanner is no longer needed. Some apps need the [LSPosed module](#lsposed-module).
- **History and favorites:** Scanned codes are kept on the phone as history, and entries can be added to favorites. Favorites stay at the top of the history and can be renamed and reordered; up to four can be added to the shortcuts shown when the FerryQR icon is long pressed.
- **Shows codes:** Tapping an entry in the history draws its code again, to be scanned by another phone or saved as an image. The code can be switched to another format to suit the reader, enlarged, and shown at full brightness, so it scans more reliably.
- **Creates codes and barcodes:** FerryQR draws every format ZXing writes and suggests the one that suits the text best. Codes are ready to share, copy or save once created.
- **Quick Settings tile:** Once added to Quick Settings, it starts scanning from the notification shade.

## Install

FerryQR needs Android 11 or later on a 64-bit ARM phone. Download the APK from [Releases](https://github.com/lcebot/ferryqr/releases).

## LSPosed module

Some codes lead to a feature or page inside an app only when that app's own scanner reads them. With FerryQR enabled as an LSPosed module, FerryQR ferries their content straight into those apps, so one scanner does what is otherwise spread across them. Without the module, FerryQR can at most open such an app's scanner for the code to be scanned again; opening the code in the browser first, for the browser to pass it on to the app, is also worth a try. DiDi, Meituan and WeChat are supported so far. Alipay, Mi Home and Xiaomi Account have entries other apps can open, so they work without the module.

1. In LSPosed, enable FerryQR and tick DiDi, Meituan and WeChat in its scope.
2. Restart those apps.
3. Open FerryQR and check in the settings, at the top left of the scanner, that the module is active for each app.

## Privacy

FerryQR has no internet access: what it scans, keeps and creates is processed and stored on the phone only, and the settings can keep codes that may hold sensitive information out of history. FerryQR asks for the permissions below for these features.

- **Camera:** Scanning with the camera. Without it, images can still be scanned, which needs no permission at all: they can be picked in FerryQR, shared to it or opened with it.
- **App list:** Finding which installed apps open a code, so result cards can offer "Open in" an app and the ferry page can show each app's status. Without it, FerryQR cannot tell which apps are installed, and those ways to open a code may not appear.
- **Wi-Fi state:** Telling whether the phone supports Wi-Fi Easy Connect. Android grants it at install without asking; on systems that can turn it off, Wi-Fi Easy Connect codes cannot be handed over without it.
- **Clipboard:** The create page reads the clipboard once, as it opens, and fills in its text automatically. Without it, the text has to be pasted by hand.

## License

[MIT](https://github.com/lcebot/ferryqr/blob/main/LICENSE). FerryQR uses [zxing-cpp](https://github.com/zxing-cpp/zxing-cpp), [ZXing](https://github.com/zxing/zxing) and [WeChatQRCode](https://github.com/jenly1314/WeChatQRCode), all licensed under Apache 2.0.
